task_message:
Case L39: segment the lipomatous soft-tissue tumor on this T1-weighted MRI.

Volume: 251x251x435 voxels, 1 mm isotropic. Budgets: max 40 tool calls / 15 model prompts / 10 min wall time.
Start with `seg_open`. Finish with `seg_finish`.
final_assistant_text:
Case L39 is complete.

**What was segmented:** a large, multilobular lipomatous soft-tissue tumor of the thigh on T1-weighted MRI — a 2663 mL fat-isointense mass with a thin capsule, displacing the surrounding musculature. It extends from the upper thigh (anterior to the hip joint, axial 130) through the mid-thigh and into a distinct round distal lobule (ending at axial 381).

**How:**
- Scanned axial/coronal/sagittal contact sheets to locate the mass and confirm it was an intramuscular/deep fatty tumor rather than normal subcutis (capsule + muscle displacement).
- Two positive point prompts on the bright core (axial 217) and on the separate-looking distal lobule (axial 340) produced a single connected component covering both parts (1642 → 2678 mL).
- Verified the ends and boundaries on multiple slices (axial 122, 130, 140, 170, 294, 300, 316, 340, 375) and on the automatic multi-planar final reviews; confirmed no tumor tissue in the past-the-mask panels.
- Rejected the three intensity-based candidate proposals (C1–C3), which were normal muscle and subcutaneous fat.
- Applied a mild morphological opening to remove ~100 tiny stray fragments (2678 → 2663 mL), leaving the main mass intact.

Final confidence: medium (boundary follows the lesion capsule in all three planes; residual uncertainty only at the irregular upper pole and a few <3 mL boundary fragments).
